title: Canonical inverse-image tensor unit on entire quotient towers
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its positive quotient coefficient rings $A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism, with the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and completed coefficient sheaves $R_X,R_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $H=g^{-1}$ be the exact completed-module inverse image with action transported through the specified coefficient isomorphism [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Write $\operatorname{Seq}_E(Y)$ for sheaves of modules over the quotient-ring sheaf on the sequence site, and $U_Y:\operatorname{Seq}_E(Y)\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y))$ for exact termwise restriction [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]; use the analogous notation on $X$. Let $g^*_{\mathrm{seq}}$ be the actual whole-system pullback with its specified adjunction unit [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Define $H_{\mathrm{tow}}$ by applying $H$ at every level and transition. There is a unique natural isomorphism $u_g:H_{\mathrm{tow}}\circ U_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X\circ g^*_{\mathrm{seq}}$ whose component, at every positive index and object $V$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, sends a section $x$ over the postcomposition $gV$ to the sequence-pullback adjunction-unit generator at $gV$, restricted along the canonical comma arrow $V\to g^*(gV)$. Equivalently it is the sheafified termwise map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, with the actual quotient transitions. Define its derived natural isomorphism by localization of these exact functors and the canonical composition isomorphisms. With $\Delta$ the constant-tower functor [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], define the identification $\Delta H\cong H_{\mathrm{tow}}\Delta$ by localizing the ordinary constant-functor/whiskering identification, identity on every component.

source.place: Definition definition-pushforward (Tag 03D6), Lemmas lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (Tag 03CZ) and lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; applied to the small sequence site of Tag 0941. Blueprint thm-trf-l-function-euler-product.proof.md, Step 1 Global powers: canonical pullback identifications.

proof.text: Use the map/pullback adjunction for the pro-etale site. Postcomposition along g is an equivalence, so its adjunction with base change is an equivalence. Take the product with the identity of the sequence index. Vertical coverings show that both product functors are continuous. The constant-section direct ring map is the sheafification compatibility isomorphism. Thus the levelwise sequence ring map is invertible, and Mathlib pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence makes the actual sequence direct image an equivalence. Its recorded left-adjoint unit is consequently invertible.

The direct constant-ring map followed by restriction along the canonical comma arrow has the defining constant-section normalization of inverseImageFiniteCoefficientMap. Uniqueness identifies these maps. The limit projection equation for inverseImageCompletedCoefficientMap then proves that the completed scalar action is respected by the sequence adjunction unit followed by comma restriction. At level n form this linear natural transformation using pushforwardNatIso and pushforwardCongr. Both its adjunction-unit and comma-restriction factors are isomorphisms.

Transport the level isomorphisms through coefficientSequenceRestriction_evaluation. Its underlying section map carries the recorded cast of x to x. Naturality of the adjunction unit and the product-site composition equations prove compatibility with every quotient transition; naturality in the sequence module is inherited from the level transformations. NatIso.ofComponents assembles the whole-tower isomorphism. Every source section is a cast of an original sequence section, so extensionality and the prescribed formula prove uniqueness. The existing derived and diagonal definitions localize these exact constructions unchanged.
